title: Quadratic Reciprocity Algorithm for Jacobi and Legendre Symbols

problemStatement.formal: A recursive Jacobi-symbol algorithm computes J(a | b), and the induced Legendre-symbol computation agrees with legendreSym for odd primes.
problemStatement.plain: Backfills metadata for the verified quadratic-reciprocity algorithm entry. The Lean file defines a recursive Jacobi-symbol computation, proves it matches the Jacobi symbol, and packages a Legendre-symbol computation for odd primes.
whyMatters: Quadratic reciprocity becomes computationally useful through algorithms for Jacobi and Legendre symbols.
The recursive proof mirrors the arithmetic reductions used by the classical symbol algorithm.
The completed termination and correctness evidence makes this a reusable number-theory algorithm entry.

proven: `jacobiAlgo_eq_jacobiSym` proves the recursive algorithm computes the Jacobi symbol up to the tracked sign flip.
`legendreCompute_eq` proves the induced computation agrees with the Legendre symbol for odd primes.
`jacobiAlgo_mod_left` records compatibility with reducing the left argument modulo the modulus.
The exact `QuadraticReciprocityAlgorithmOQ01.lean` file is recorded with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
open: Further optimization details and deeper links to factorization machinery are natural follow-ups beyond this correctness slice.
knownResults.goal: Replace empty algorithm metadata with the theorem-backed Jacobi/Legendre correctness evidence.

currentState.nextAction: Read problem.md thoroughly and acquire full context.

builtItems: Fixed jacobiAux termination proof (replaced sorry with strip2_snd_le + omega)
insights: Existing file implements full Jacobi symbol algorithm with strip2, jacobiAux, jacobi functions
Had 1 sorry in termination proof for jacobiAux
Termination key: odd_part = (strip2 (a%n)).2 <= a%n < n, so odd_part < n
Added strip2_snd_le lemma: (strip2 n).2 <= n by strong induction
Used strip2_snd_le to fix termination via Prod.Lex.left
nextSteps: Prove correctness: jacobi a p = legendreSym p a for odd primes p
